subject: blueprintSpitfire
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: Spitfire fighter plane.
Style: cyanotype blueprint.
reasoning:
I'm planning a cyanotype blueprint-style Spitfire model, aiming for efficient code with a static plane resting on its landing gear, roughly matching real dimensions like a 9.1m length and 11.2m wingspan.

For the look, I'm going with deep blue fuselage colors broken up by white panel lines and grid seams, plus SVG-based roundels and labels to sell the blueprint aesthetic. I'm sketching out the construction plan: lofting the fuselage along the z-axis through a series of width/height stations from tail to nose, lathing a nose cone and spinner, adding a glowing canopy sphere, and extruding elliptical wing profiles with the right thickness axis orientation.

Now I'm refining the wing outline points to get a Spitfire-style elliptical shape with a wide root chord tapering to a rounded tip, adjusting thickness and dihedral by tweaking the direction vectors, and planning similarly smaller extrusions for the tailplane and fin.

Then I'm sketching the remaining details: a three-blade rotating propeller with a spinner cone, exhaust stacks, wing guns, radiator box, landing gear legs with wheels, a tailwheel, and roundel decals placed on the wings and fuselage sides.

Working out the gear placement now: wheels at the wing roots, legs angling down to the ground, plus a tail wheel positioned under the rear fuselage to keep everything grounded properly.

Now I'm figuring out surface detailing with a paint function that shades by normal direction and adds panel lines across the fuselage and wing ribs.

I'm also planning decal textures — an SVG roundel, a serial number on the tail fin, and maybe canopy frame stripes — then settling on a simple color palette to start writing the actual code.

Now I'm defining the fuselage loft stations as a series of width/height cross-sections from nose to tail, then moving on to shaping the engine cowl with a lathe geometry.

Still writing spinner and prop blade outlines...

Now I'm placing exhaust cylinders along the cowl sides, gun barrel rods extending from the wings, and radiator boxes mounted underneath.

For the canopy, I'm scaling a sphere into an elongated dome and adding thin white box frame bars across it instead of a textured decal. I'm also writing a shared paint helper for the wing surfaces based on their upward-facing normals, then mirroring the wing outline geometry across the x-axis for the opposite side.

Now I'm shifting to the tail assembly: defining the tailplane outline points near the rear fuselage, extruding the fin shape upward from a slightly forward position, and setting its thickness. I'm planning to use textured planes for the roundel decals on the wings, fuselage sides, and fin serial markings rather than modeling them as geometry.

Positioning roundels on the fuselage by computing the half-width at that z-depth, then placing mirrored decals symmetrically on both sides while making sure fin text isn't flipped by using the correct facing direction for each side.
